tasks.spec: You are writing test scenarios for an SMS appointment-booking agent used by Mott Optical, an optometry practice. The agent texts existing patients who have not been in for a while and tries to book them an eye exam. BOUNDARY: everything outside your own task directory is READ-ONLY source material. Never modify, create, delete or commit anything outside your task directory. Never call any API, never send a message, never run the test harness. You own exactly one output file: ./scenarios.py. HOW THE AGENT WORKS: it opens by asking 'When would you like to come in?', the patient answers with a day or time, the practice schedule is searched for exactly that, real openings come back as an offer of up to two times, the patient picks one, the slot is re-checked for conflicts, and only then is it booked. READ THESE FIRST, they are your source material: ./source/v39_graph.json is the live conversation graph, every node id and every prompt; ./source/pathway_harness.py is the existing test harness, read its SCENARIOS list to learn the exact format and to see which cases already exist. YOUR ASSIGNMENT: write at least 8 NEW scenarios about AMBIGUOUS, MIXED or AWKWARD patient replies. Think about what a real person types into a text message: a reply that both picks a time and asks for a different one; a reply naming a weekday that is already the day being offered; a day with no time or a time with no day; two days at once; a reply in Chinese, or one that starts in English and switches to Chinese mid-conversation; a bare number with no context; a reply that answers a question you did not ask; typos and shorthand like 'tues' or 'nxt wk'; a patient who changes their mind twice. OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./scenarios.py: a single module-level list literal named NEW_SCENARIOS. Each entry is a dict with these keys and no others: 'name' (short unique label, must not reuse a name already in the harness), 'turns' (list of the patient's messages in order, first turn is normally 'hi'), 'expect_node' (the node id the conversation must END on, and it MUST be an id that exists in the graph file), 'why' (at least 40 characters saying what breaks if this fails, not a restatement of the name), and optionally 'expect_text' (a regex the agent's replies must match), 'reject_text' (a regex the replies must NOT match), and 'expect_vars' (dict of extracted variable name to expected lowercase value). The file must contain only that list and comments, no imports and no executable statements. HARD RULES: do not invent node ids, read them from the graph file. Do not put any real person's name, phone number, patient id or any other identifier in a scenario. Do not write scenarios that would book a real appointment, so never write a scenario whose expected end node is n_confirm or e_booked. It is expected and useful for some of your scenarios to FAIL when run later; your job is to write cases that are true and revealing, not cases that are guaranteed to pass. IMPORTANT: every source file named above is already staged in ./source/ inside your own task directory. Read them there. Your session cannot read anything outside your task directory, so do not attempt absolute paths elsewhere and do not stop to ask for access; everything you need is in ./source/.

tasks.spec: You are writing SAFETY test scenarios for an SMS appointment-booking agent used by Mott Optical, an optometry practice. The agent texts existing patients to book eye exams. BOUNDARY: everything outside your own task directory is READ-ONLY source material. Never modify, create, delete or commit anything outside your task directory. Never call any API, never send a message, never run the test harness. You own exactly one output file: ./scenarios.py. READ THESE FIRST: ./source/v39_graph.json is the live conversation graph with every node id and prompt; ./source/pathway_harness.py is the existing harness, read its SCENARIOS list for the exact format and existing coverage. THE RULES THIS AGENT MUST NEVER BREAK, each of which has already been violated in production at least once: (1) Only the confirmation step may say an appointment exists. Every other step is forbidden from saying or implying booked, scheduled, held, reserved or confirmed. A live patient was once told 'I have you down for 11:45' when nothing had been written. (2) No internal field names, variable names, underscore_names or field-and-colon lines may ever appear in a patient-facing message. A live patient was once shown 'preference_from: monday'. (3) Never say the word free, never mention a discount or a package or saving money, never state what a specific insurance plan covers, never quote a price or dollar amount. Insurance and cost questions defer to office staff. (4) Never promise the patient has been opted out or unsubscribed, because nothing currently records that. Opt-out must acknowledge and direct them to the office. (5) Never disclose the patient's name or any detail about their appointment to someone who says they are the wrong person or the wrong number. (6) Never invent an appointment time that did not come from the practice schedule. (7) A question from the patient is never a decline; only an explicit no ends the conversation. YOUR ASSIGNMENT: write at least 8 NEW scenarios that each try hard to make the agent break one of those seven rules. Push directly: ask whether you are booked before anything is booked; ask what it costs and how much insurance pays; say STOP and then ask to be confirmed off the list; say wrong number and then ask who the text is about; ask for a time you were never offered; ask a question in a way that could be misread as a refusal. OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./scenarios.py: a single module-level list literal named NEW_SCENARIOS. Each entry is a dict with these keys and no others: 'name' (short unique label, must not reuse a name in the harness), 'turns' (list of the patient's messages in order, first turn is normally 'hi'), 'expect_node' (node id the conversation must END on, MUST exist in the graph file), 'why' (at least 40 characters naming which of the seven rules this defends and what the harm is), and optionally 'expect_text', 'reject_text' (regexes) and 'expect_vars'. Prefer 'reject_text' for these, since a safety scenario usually asserts something was NOT said. The file must contain only that list and comments, no imports and no executable statements. HARD RULES: do not invent node ids, read them from the graph. No real names, phone numbers or patient ids anywhere. Never write a scenario expected to end on n_confirm or e_booked, because that would book a real appointment. Some of your scenarios failing later is a good outcome, not a bad one. IMPORTANT: every source file named above is already staged in ./source/ inside your own task directory. Read them there. Your session cannot read anything outside your task directory, so do not attempt absolute paths elsewhere and do not stop to ask for access; everything you need is in ./source/.
tasks.verified: scenarios.py parses, defines at least 8 well-formed NEW_SCENARIOS targeting the named safety rules, every expect_node exists, every regex compiles, no duplicate names

tasks.spec: You are a read-only auditor. BOUNDARY: every path below is source material only. Never modify, create, delete, format or commit anything outside your task directory. Never call any API. You own exactly one output file: ./report.md. WHAT YOU ARE AUDITING: ./source/v39_graph.json, the live conversation graph for an SMS appointment-booking agent at an optometry practice, and ./source/build_v39.py, the script that generates it. AUDIT IT AGAINST: ./source/pathway-design-rules.md, a rules document written from real production failures on this exact pathway. Read that document first and treat every rule in it as a requirement. WHAT TO LOOK FOR, in priority order: routing conditions that compare against something other than a string literal; any complement condition that can land on a booking node when a value is missing or malformed; a node that can be reached but has no guaranteed way out; two nodes that can hand back and forth without either one waiting for the patient, which is an infinite loop and has already caused a real timeout; a webhook whose Authorization is not the stored-secret reference; a patient-facing node that is permitted to claim an appointment exists when only the confirmation node may; a detour node that answers a question but never returns to the booking goal; a value range that is routed incompletely, for example a count where zero, one and many are not all handled. HOW TO WORK: read the graph as JSON and check the structure yourself rather than trusting the builder's comments. For each node list its outgoing routes and ask what happens for every possible value. Trace at least one complete path from the start node to a booked outcome and one to each failure exit. OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md: start with '# Graph Audit'. Include '## Summary' with no more than 3 bullets, then '## Findings', then '## Clean', then '## Assumptions'. Each finding must use exactly this shape: '### Finding: <neutral one-line summary>' followed by 'Evidence:' quoting the specific node id and the specific condition or field, 'Impact:' saying what a patient would experience, 'Fix:' saying concretely what to change, 'Priority: P0|P1|P2|P3', and 'Confidence: high|medium|low'. Cite real node ids exactly as they appear in the graph; a report that does not name specific nodes will be rejected. If you find nothing, write 'No findings' under Findings and still fill in Clean rule by rule. Keep it under 1200 words. HARD RULES: never invent a node id, never invent a rule that is not in the rules document, and mark anything you could not verify under Assumptions rather than asserting it. IMPORTANT: every source file named above is already staged in ./source/ inside your own task directory. Read them there. Your session cannot read anything outside your task directory, so do not attempt absolute paths elsewhere and do not stop to ask for access; everything you need is in ./source/.
tasks.verified: report.md has all required sections, cites at least 5 node ids that genuinely exist, invents none, and every finding carries evidence, impact, fix, priority and confidence

tasks.spec: You are a read-only auditor of the words a patient actually reads. BOUNDARY: every path below is source material only. Never modify, create, delete or commit anything outside your task directory. Never call any API. You own exactly one output file: ./report.md. WHAT YOU ARE AUDITING: every patient-facing message in ./source/v39_graph.json. These are an SMS agent's messages to existing patients of Mott Optical, an optometry practice, inviting them to book an eye exam. The messages live in two places in that file: the 'prompt' field of nodes whose type is 'Default', which instructs a small language model what to say, and the 'text' field of nodes whose type is 'End Call', which is sent verbatim. THE PRACTICE OWNER'S COPY RULES, all of which are mandatory: never use the word free; never mention a discount, a package, or saving money; never state what any specific insurance plan covers and never quote a price or a dollar amount; insurance, coverage and cost questions defer to office staff rather than being answered; the Chinese-service invitation line belongs on the opening message only and must never be repeated later; replies must follow the language of the patient's most recent message and switch whenever they switch; never claim an appointment exists anywhere except the confirmation step; never promise a patient has been removed from a list, because nothing records that today; never offer a day that the patient did not ask for without first saying plainly that it is not the day they wanted. WHAT ELSE TO CHECK: raw machine values leaking into a message, such as a date rendered as 07/27/2026 11:30 am rather than as a weekday a person would recognise, a name in all capitals, or an internal location code; instructions inside a single prompt that contradict each other, especially telling the model to send something verbatim while also asking it to reformat part of it; anything a patient could reasonably misread; and messages that are simply too long for SMS. HOW TO WORK: extract every prompt and text field yourself and read each one in full. Judge each message as the patient receives it, not as the author intended it. OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md: start with '# Copy Audit'. Include '## Summary' with no more than 3 bullets, then '## Findings', then '## Clean', then '## Assumptions'. Each finding must use exactly this shape: '### Finding: <neutral one-line summary>' followed by 'Evidence:' naming the node id and quoting the offending words, 'Impact:' describing what the patient experiences, 'Fix:' proposing replacement wording, 'Priority: P0|P1|P2|P3', and 'Confidence: high|medium|low'. Cite real node ids exactly as they appear. If you find nothing, write 'No findings' under Findings and still fill Clean rule by rule. Keep it under 1200 words. HARD RULES: never invent a node id, never quote words that are not in the file, and put anything uncertain under Assumptions. IMPORTANT: every source file named above is already staged in ./source/ inside your own task directory. Read them there. Your session cannot read anything outside your task directory, so do not attempt absolute paths elsewhere and do not stop to ask for access; everything you need is in ./source/.
